topic: Managed AI agents for real work (Grok @Bot)
angle: Managed agents only work when you shrink the problem and expand the guardrails.
linkedinPost:
AI “teammates” won’t replace your team. They’ll force you to define work precisely.

Latent Space’s writeup on Grok @Bot frames the next wave: managed agents that tackle real tasks, not just chat. That’s the right direction—but the boring details decide if these ship or stall.

My take from FDE work: managed agents only work when you shrink the problem and expand the guardrails. We get wins by giving agents a tight task catalog, bounded tools, time budgets, and crisp handoff rules. “General assistant” fails quietly; “triage refund requests under $100 with policy X, escalate Y” succeeds.

We also log everything like a flight recorder: tool calls, intermediate thoughts, timeouts, retries. Then we run red-team scripts weekly to break them on purpose. Two numbers matter: containment rate (tasks finished without human) and bad-escalation rate (when they asked for help but shouldn’t have).

A recent Latent Space piece highlights the market moment. The craft is in operational design: scoping, observability, and rollback paths.

If you’re piloting agents this quarter, what’s your smallest high-frequency task you’d trust to a bot first? #ForwardDeployedEngineer #AIEngineering #LLM #CustomerEngineering
xPost: Agents work when you shrink scope and expand guardrails. Task catalogs, bounded tools, time budgets, audit logs—then track containment vs bad‑escalation rate. “General assistant” fails; specific workflows win. Start tiny, high‑frequency. #AIEngineering #LLM
